own_solution.law: Calorimetry, heat lost by copper = heat gained by water: dT_water = m_c c_c (T_c - T_w)/(m_c c_c + m_w c_w)
assumptions: perfectly insulated container that absorbs no heat (stated)

notes: m_c c_c = 192.5 J/K, m_w c_w = 1674.4 J/K; rise = 192.5*80/1866.9 = 8.24897 K (final 301.249 K). With 0.95 kg water: m_w c_w = 3976.7 J/K, rise = 15400/4169.2 = 3.69375 K. Earlier-experiment sentences are D (the problem states nothing from any other experiment is left); second-container sentences are D. TDD5D and T4800 add water at 293 K to the first container before the block, so R. T128A/TDD5D and TCCED/T4800 are word-level variants with the same 0.55 kg. TD942 and TC375 say 'a small amount' with no number; if meant as variants of numbered sentences they differ in the number, to check in pass 2.
